title: Biometric Collection & Use Safeguards Pattern
description: A pattern combining documented informed consent at every biometric collection point with independent human confirmation before any biometric match triggers an adverse action, and demographic-disaggregated accuracy testing before deployment.
problem: Biometric systems fail in two distinct, equally serious ways: data is collected without the individual's knowledge or consent (as with images scraped from the public web), and matches are acted upon automatically without independent human confirmation, compounding any accuracy or bias problem in the underlying model.
solution: Require documented, informed consent before any biometric identifier is collected or processed, regardless of source; test match accuracy and false-positive rate separately across demographic groups before deployment; and require a trained human to independently confirm any match before it triggers an adverse action against an individual.
applicability: Any system that collects, stores, or matches biometric identifiers — facial recognition, fingerprint, voiceprint, or iris/retina systems — whether for security, loss-prevention, authentication, or law-enforcement support.
consequences: Consent-gating scraped or third-party data sources can be operationally difficult to retrofit onto an existing dataset; mandatory human confirmation adds latency and staffing cost to systems designed for real-time response.
